evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 漢字甲骨部件分析; 形義通解
evidence.text: The database interprets 面’s oracle forms as a facial outline enclosing an eye and gives ‘face’ as the original sense. It reports that 面 itself is not attested in bronze inscriptions, though a related bronze graph uses 𦣻 with an enclosure. It also reports a Chu-slip enclosure altered toward 臼 and cites 面 ‘face toward’ in 上博楚竹書二《容成氏》簡14. These are the database’s analyses and reported citations; no artifact was independently inspected here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 面

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》, Taiwan Ministry of Education
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; 釋義
evidence.text: The entry says 麵 is written 麪 in Shuowen, analyzed as 麥 semantic plus 丏 phonetic and glossed 麥末也. It says 麵 later became a common writing and that 玉篇 and 廣韻 equate 麵 and 麪. The cited literary examples do not establish the first date of the flour or noodle senses.
evidence.title: A04763 麵 — 教育部《異體字字典》

The page releases the SVG representation into the public domain and lists 麥 and 丏 as components. This is a modern drawing, not an artifact image. The exact original-file link was opened, but the web tool returned a cache-miss error.

search_audit.query: 面 oracle bone character form evolution face CUHK 甲骨文字形; Commons 面-seal.svg 麵-seal.svg Shuowen seal; Ministry dictionary 麵 麪 麥 丏
search_audit.outcome: Inspected CUHK’s 面 paleographic record, Ministry entries for 面 and 麵, and exact Commons pages for 面-seal.svg and 麵-seal.svg. The 面 seal original URL returned a fetch error; 麵 seal original URL returned cache miss. The proposed radical-file description page was inaccessible, so that lead was not selected.

gaps: The individual oracle inscriptions and their dates were not verified; the face interpretation is CUHK’s scholarly analysis. The database reports no bronze inscription of 面 itself but does not specify the coverage limits for this claim.

The Chu-slip form change toward 臼 and reported ‘face toward’ example were not independently checked against the slip. Dates and semantic links among facing, surface, side and dimension remain unresolved.

The Ministry dictionary supports 麪, its 麥-plus-丏 analysis, and later 麵 spelling, but does not establish the transition chronology or separate earliest written attestations for flour and noodle senses.

The direct Commons image requests for both selected redraws failed in the web tool. Their identity, modern-redrawing status and reuse terms are supported by their inspected description pages; pixels were not inspected here.
The Shuowen-style label describes the script style of modern vector redraws and does not prove these images reproduce a specific excavated or manuscript specimen.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; associated with the transmitted Shuowen tradition, not a dated artifact
items.caption: A modern vector rendering of 面 in Shuowen seal-script style. The face graph is interpreted in the CUHK database as an outline enclosing an eye.
items.alt: Black seal-script form of 面, shown as a modern vector drawing.
items.selection_reason: Shows a later script-style form of the entry character after the reported oracle-bone pictograph; helps distinguish a modern redraw from an artifact photograph.
items.rights: Public domain, as stated on the Commons description page; attribution appreciated but not required.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; the dictionary identifies 麪 as the Shuowen form and 麵 as a later common spelling
items.caption: A modern vector rendering of 麵 in Shuowen seal-script style. The Ministry dictionary records 麪 as the Shuowen graph, with 麥 for meaning and 丏 for sound, and 麵 as a later writing.
items.alt: Black seal-script form labeled 麵, shown as a modern vector drawing.
items.selection_reason: Illustrates the separate flour/food graph history relevant to distinguishing 面’s face graph from 麵 and its simplified writing use; the caption preserves the source’s caveat that this redraw is associated with the 面 page.
items.rights: Public domain, as stated on the Commons description page; attribution appreciated but not required.

limitations.text: Both candidates are modern vector redrawings, not photographs or direct facsimiles of dated artifacts. Their exact original-file links were established through the inspected Commons pages but could not be fetched by the web tool, so the pixels were not inspected.
